g.text: A write reaches 2 of 3 copies; a later read queries a different 2 of 3 -- and still finds it.
Write acks from A and B: W=2 reached. Node C never even needed to answer.
READ (R = 2 of N = 3), a different pair
Node B answers both the write and this read: the shared replica is what guarantees the read sees value=42.
W + R = 2 + 2 = 4 > N = 3. By the pigeonhole principle, the write set and the read set
cannot be fully disjoint -- they must share at least one node, and that node has the latest value.
